decisions: Took the shared read path (the bigger fix) and moved the rest off the thread with F2's floor. The read path is opt-in per read (read_beside.first / observer operations of read scope), never global: a read that tries to write is refused by SQLite (query_only; a BEGIN IMMEDIATE/EXCLUSIVE is refused before SQLite) and made again under the guard, so code that writes while reading (tables made on first use, a failed nested read's audit) still works as before.

How the journal (K1) was checked: (1) a reader can never write (query_only), so the journal's 'sent' and 'confirmed' records are still written only under the guard, one writer at a time across threads and processes; (2) resume, a step's verification, a grant's check and every press are write operations and keep reading under the guard; (3) smoke: a three-step Rail Demo assignment run while a reader read assignment.status beside every step: every view was a prefix of the final journal, a step read as done always had its DONE record in the same view, each effect sent once and done once; reads beside an open write see the last committed value; one block reads one snapshot; (4) K1's own smoke (kill before/after the effect, resume, Stop, Stop all) 30/30 on the F2b code.

Both modes: the reads beside are in Kernel.db, which the Ledger service's client inherits (the window's direct reads), and the service lets observer reads past its dispatch lock (checked in-process on its Coordinator with the lock held as by a step in flight: a read 1-2 ms, a write waited for the lock).

Readers are kept open per thread (one per database): opening a connection reads the whole schema again (183 tables and indexes on Rail Demo). A kept reader has its row and text factories reset before each block and is dropped when the database file is not the one it opened (device and inode).

The Office catalogue object is kept per catalogue file (path, device, inode): constructing it ran the catalogue's schema and defaults under BEGIN IMMEDIATE on the profile's catalog database at every office.get, so the window's and the workers' office.get waited on each other; a catalogue made afresh or put back is checked again as before.

The Field: a re-show keeps its drawing and reads on a worker; a window that did not open on the Field reads the desk on a worker as soon as it is up and the first show takes that reading (read again on a worker when the journal moved since). A forced refresh (after the owner's act, R) stays synchronous, as its callers read what changed right after.

The 0.8.x assignment's row has no bar and no time left (the old loop keeps neither): its state word is the old path's own (running, ready, paused, needs you) with a shape, its line the steps it took, its Stop agent.stop on its id, a click on its title says agent.status's words. Nothing steps or resumes it from there.
GRAPHITE_READ_BESIDE=0 turns all of it off (every read under the guard, writes on the window's thread) for the owner's comparison on the ThinkPad; GRAPHITE_STALL_LOG (F2) measures it there.

The smoke measures as F2 did (same flow, restore=False, the harness's own reads left out); numbers are from this shared, niced 4-core container with other builders beside, three runs each, interleaved before/after.
findings_for_the_coordinator: Remaining over 100 ms (Day, after): the window's own work, none of it a wait on her writes: the owner's tile click (the board's rebuild: ~20 Kernel reads now beside her plus the layout, the tree's reveal saving the profile file, the dispatch's schema table), the board's first build after the Field (to_board), her column drawing NEXT STEPS' buttons when a reading lands, the rings' picture redrawn once per focus change, the tree's placement on the type bar's align. Each is 100-130 ms here under nice 19 with other builders' processes; a click is about 45 ms of the window's own work under the profiler (three clicks: 140 ms). Next steps if the owner's ThinkPad shows them: build the board off the thread (bm.build on a worker from the desk reading, drawn when it lands) and keep NEXT STEPS' buttons instead of making them anew each drawing.

Every Kernel.dispatch reads the workspace's marker file (project_context.detached -> locations.marker: a stat, an open and a JSON parse) and validates against engineering_cli.schemas(): on the window's thread these are the most sampled frames left in a click. A per-root cache keyed by the marker's mtime would take them out.

activity.status() still counts the whole activity journal and globs three folders; stacy_awareness.inspect calls it; the timeline now reads it on a worker (when the journal moved, else every 4th tick), but other callers still pay it.

office_service is not the only store made per call: notebook_service.store and notes_exchange make a fresh Catalog (schema and defaults under BEGIN IMMEDIATE) per call too; the same keeping would serve them.

In the Graphite and Kasandra looks the left tree's branch drawing (draw_branches, draw_wires: Python per row, 64 rows) remains 100-150 ms under load once in a run; the words' light is now a kept picture (a breath 6-18 ms with 64 rows).

Its assertion is still true (it reads the receipt an earlier tick wrote while settle() ran); if it ever reads too early, a settle after the call fixes it. Not changed, not run (the owner's rule).
F2's drill showed the 0.8.7 window's old Work driver adopting the running 0.8.x assignment; listing it in ACTIVE WORK does not change that (agent_qt still steps it as 0.8.7 did).
